analysis.evidence: בִּשְׁנַת introduces the date, and שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה לְחַיֵּי נֹחַ identifies it as the six hundredth year of Noah’s life. The following month and day locate the event within that year.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בִּ־ ‘in’ prefixed to שְׁנַת, the feminine singular construct of שָׁנָה.

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת, שֵׁשׁ counts the hundreds. The phrase dates the event to the six hundredth year of Noah’s life.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: six as the multiplier in six hundred

analysis.evidence: שֵׁשׁ counts the hundreds in שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, “six hundred years.” The phrase dates the event to the six hundredth year of Noah’s life.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the singular שָׁנָה gives the unit counted by “six hundred.” The following לְחַיֵּי נֹחַ identifies these as years of Noah’s life, dating the event to his six hundredth year.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: The construct חַיֵּי takes נֹחַ as its possessor. The phrase לְחַיֵּי נֹחַ identifies the six hundredth year as a year of Noah’s life.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine plural construct noun.
analysis.sense: lifetime, the days of one's life

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In לְחַיֵּי נֹחַ, “of Noah’s life,” נֹחַ names the person whose six hundredth year dates the flood.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי means “in the second month.” The verse then specifies the seventeenth day of that month, confirming the calendar sense.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי, “in the second month,” הַשֵּׁנִי agrees with חֹדֶשׁ in gender, number, and definiteness and gives the month’s position in the year.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute ordinal adjective.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעָה combines with the following עָשָׂר to form ‘seventeen’. The counted noun יוֹם is masculine, and בְּ marks the date as ‘on the seventeenth day of the month’.
analysis.morphology: Temporal preposition בְּ (‘on’) prefixed to שִׁבְעָה, the masculine singular absolute form of the cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, שִׁבְעָה supplies seven and עָשָׂר supplies ten. Together they specify the seventeenth day of the month.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral, the second element of שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, the numeral seventeen counts days of the month, giving the date ‘on the seventeenth day of the month.’
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי identifies the second month. In בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, the marked word refers back to that month and specifies that the date is its seventeenth day.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition לְ and definite article הַ, combined as לַ־.

analysis.evidence: In בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה, the demonstrative הַזֶּה points back to the seventeenth day of the second month. The phrase places the bursting of the springs and the opening of the floodgates on that same day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed בְּ ‘on’ and the definite article הַ, contracted to בַּ־.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb נִבְקְעוּ agrees with its following subject כָּל מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה, “all the springs of the great deep.” The parallel clause says that the floodgates of heaven “were opened” (נִפְתָּחוּ). Both clauses describe sources of floodwater opening.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: כָּל quantifies the plural מַעְיְנֹת in כָּל מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה. All the springs of the great deep are the subject of נִבְקְעוּ, “burst open.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מַעְיְנֹת is in construct with תְּהוֹם רַבָּה, yielding “springs of the great deep.” These springs burst open (נִבְקְעוּ) as the floodgates of heaven open.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה means “the springs of the great deep.” The springs burst open as the windows of the heavens open, pairing floodwaters from below with water from above.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement in רַבָּה.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה, “all the springs of the great deep,” רַבָּה agrees with the feminine singular תְּהוֹם and describes the vast extent of the deep.
analysis.morphology: Attributive adjective, feminine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: אֲרֻבֹּת is in construct with הַשָּׁמַיִם, giving “the windows of heaven.” The verb נִפְתָּחוּ (“were opened”) parallels the bursting open of the springs of the deep. In this flood scene, “floodgates” conveys the function of the heavenly openings.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ־ plus feminine plural construct noun, with no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲרֻבֹּת הַשָּׁמַיִם נִפְתָּחוּ, “and the floodgates of the sky were opened,” הַשָּׁמַיִם identifies where the floodgates are. The verse pairs the waters above with the springs of the great deep below.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb נִפְתָּחוּ agrees with אֲרֻבֹּת הַשָּׁמַיִם, “the floodgates of heaven.” Its passive sense parallels נִבְקְעוּ, “were split open,” in the preceding clause about the springs of the deep.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural
